options.why_wrong: 'So' introduces a result clause. The absolute phrase expresses circumstance, so this joins the two parts with the wrong logical relation.

if the students had left the room.
options.why_wrong: A conditional clause does not complete an absolute phrase that describes the circumstances of the main action.
This has no finite main clause with a subject and verb, so it is a fragment and cannot complete the sentence.

explanation: A verbless absolute clause has its own subject, here 'the exam', and gives background circumstances. The main clause that follows needs its own subject and finite verb to form a complete sentence.
